author: Inside Edition
description: College sophomores Kyla Lemons and Jaelyn Hanna spent 100 hours turning their dorm room at the University of Alabama into a deluxe room. It is part of a new social media trend where college kids make over their dorm rooms taking them from drab to fab. In Dallas, sophomore Addison Standley had the help of her mother, who is an interior designer. The mom overhauled a room for Standley and her roommate at Nelson University.
title: Some College Students Are Turning Their Dorm Rooms From Drab To Fab

author: Inside Edition
description: Ryder Williams was honored at the White House Monday. President Donald Trump hailed the 16-year-old lifeguard, whose heroism last month captivated the nation. Williams rescued 10-year-old Nathaniel Rai in Santa Cruz, California. The video went viral and caught the attention of the president. Rai was also at the White House. Meanwhile, conservative South Carolina firebrand Nancy Mace is causing a stir after revealing her colorful new arm tattoos.
title: 16-Year-Old Lifeguard Ryder Williams Honored By President Trump At White House

author: Inside Edition
description: In the latest street take-over, a staggering 150 cars commandeered roads in south Los Angeles. Last week an Auto Zone was looted, this week a liquor store was targeted. From inside the liquor store, looters could be seen on surveillance using a power saw to cut through locks before dozens of thieves poured in. The store owners told Inside Edition it took them a decade to build their business only to have it destroyed in a matter of minutes. Police are now cracking down.
title: Looters Target Liquor Store In Street Takeover

author: Inside Edition
description: Record flooding hit Indianapolis and surrounding areas over the weekend, leaving several dead. Frank Grounder, who was hoping to celebrate his 37th birthday on Sunday, was instead surveying everything he lost. The furniture maker, who lives on the city’s north side, less than a mile from the overflowing White River, was at home watching as floodwaters crept up his driveway and into his home and workshop. Now he’s slogging through two feet of water , trying to salvage his belongings and his creations.
title: Indianapolis Furniture Maker Loses Everything in Historic Flooding on 37th Birthday

author: Inside Edition
description: She has a face you won't forget, and now has the title to prove it. Jinny Lu is the winner of The World’s Ugliest Dog Contest. The event took place at the Sonoma County Fair in Santa Rosa, California, with dogs from all over the world competing. Along with her new title, she and her human, Michelle Grady, won $5,000. The event is a good time, but it also raises awareness of the benefits of adopting rescue dogs. Inside Edition Digital has more.
title: Dog Saved From Harsh Conditions Becomes World's Ugliest Dog Winner

author: Inside Edition
description: Bodycam footage released by the New York State Police shows the race against time one trooper faced as he rescued an 80-year-old man from a burning home. On August 13, Trooper James P. Bertram got on his hands and knees and told the man inside to follow the sound of his voice. His advice worked and he was able to help the man get out. The man was taken to a nearby hospital to be treated for non-life threatening injuries.
title: Pulse-Pounding Bodycam Footage Shows Cop Saving Elderly Man from House Fire

author: Inside Edition
description: Authorities in Italy were able to recover masterpieces by Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse that were taken from a private museum near the northern city of Parma in March. The Carabinieri’s art recovery squad said in a statement that the paintings were discovered during searches ordered by prosecutors, but no further details were given. The three recovered paintings are “Fish” by Auguste Renoir, “Still Life with Cherries” by Paul Cézanne, and “Odalisque on the Terrace” by Henri Matisse. All three are worth a combined $34 million dollars.
title: Italian Authorities Recover $34M in Stolen Art After Heist Was Caught on Camera

author: Inside Edition
description: She's 100 years old with no plans to give up her adrenaline rush. Great-grandmother Ruby McNally of California celebrated her milestone birthday by jumping out of a plane. It's not like anyone could stop her. It's also how she celebrated her 80th and 90th birthdays. She tells CBS News the kids can't keep up with her. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: 100-Year-Old Great-Grandmother Celebrates Birthday By Skydiving
